unit.title: Describing Words, More Verbs, and a Longer Story

contentBlocks.text: ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਨਵੇਂ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਸਿੱਖੇ। ਅੱਜ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰੇ ਵਾਕਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਰਤੋ! (Yesterday you learned new words. Today, use them in full sentences!)

Add a describing word into last week's 'who + action' pattern: 'ਵੱਡਾ ਕੁੱਤਾ ਦੌੜਦਾ ਹੈ' (the big dog runs). 'ਛੋਟੀ ਬਿੱਲੀ ਸੋਹਣੀ ਹੈ' (the small cat is beautiful). Notice ਦੌੜਦਾ (runs) is a new verb — ਦੌੜਨਾ means 'to run.' Build your own sentence: pick ਕੁੱਤਾ or ਬਿੱਲੀ, add ਵੱਡਾ/ਵੱਡੀ or ਛੋਟਾ/ਛੋਟੀ, and say if it runs (ਦੌੜਦਾ/ਦੌੜਦੀ).
ਤੁਸੀਂ ਵਰਣਨਾਤਮਕ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਵਾਕ ਬਣਾਏ! (You just built sentences with describing words!) Tomorrow we'll learn two more new verbs.

objectives: Combine a describing word with a noun and a verb into one complete sentence
Introduce the new verb ਦੌੜਨਾ (to run) in context
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's describing words and animal nouns.
2. Model the two example sentences together, pointing out gender agreement across all three words.
3. Have the child build and say their own describing-word sentence.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's two new verbs.
differentiationTips: Struggling: build the sentence one word at a time (noun, then describing word, then verb) rather than all at once
Ready for more: ask the child to build a second sentence using the other animal noun
Gender agreement across three words (noun-adjective-verb) is the hardest part of this lesson — model it explicitly and don't rush past it
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended sentence-building activity — check that the child's sentence correctly matches gender across the noun, describing word, and verb (e.g., ਵੱਡਾ ਕੁੱਤਾ ਦੌੜਦਾ ਹੈ, all masculine forms).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'building sentences' goal, extending last week's who+action pattern with a describing word — a genuine step up in sentence complexity.

generationData.instructions: Write your own sentence using a describing word, an animal, and a verb.
